column1: # Known non-green outcomes in the `porffor-cli` test targets.
# This file is TRACKED and LOAD-BEARING. `tests/cli/known_failures.rs` pulls it
# in with `include_str!`, so deleting it, renaming it, or letting a `.gitignore`
# rule swallow it is a compile error at `cargo check --all-targets` rather than
# a silent regression.
# HAZARD, and the reason this file is `.tsv`: `.gitignore` line 3 is a bare
# `*.txt`. An earlier revision of this ledger was written as
# `known-failures.txt`, `git add -A` dropped it without a word, and the
# references in `README.md` and `docs/rust-rewrite/batch-workflow.md` outlived
# the file they pointed at for three batches. Before adding ANY tracked data
# file, run `git check-ignore -v <path>` and require exit status 1. `.tsv` is
# also this repository's existing convention for hand-maintained tables -- see
# `test262/backlog/ownership-map.tsv` and
# `test262/backlog/shortcut-allowlist.tsv`.
# A row here is a DECLARATION, not a skip. AGENTS.md bans permanent skip lists
# and silent expected failures, so every row carries an owner task and a reason,
# and the outcome is enforced by libtest itself rather than by anyone
# remembering to compare against a list:
#   fail / hang -> the named test carries `should_panic` with a NON-EMPTY
#                  `expected` substring. The suite goes RED if the test starts
#                  passing ("test did not panic as expected") and RED if it
#                  fails for a different reason (message mismatch). Both delta
#                  directions, no end-of-run machinery.
#   ignored     -> the named test carries an `ignore` attribute with a reason.
#                  `known_failures::every_ignored_test_is_declared` rejects any
#                  ignore attribute in these targets that has no row here, and
#                  any row here whose test is no longer ignored.
#   unfilled    -> a placeholder for a failure set nobody has measured yet. The
#                  test column must be exactly `UNFILLED`, and the expiry header
#                  below stops it from becoming permanent.
# The expiry header is compared against `CURRENT_BATCH` in
# `tests/cli/known_failures.rs`. When `CURRENT_BATCH` reaches the batch named
# there, any surviving `unfilled` row fails `ledger_is_well_formed`. Extending
# the deadline is possible but shows up as a diff on this line.
# unfilled-allowed-until: batch-8
# Columns, tab-separated, sorted ascending by (target, test) and unique on that
# pair. Every column must be non-empty and carry no leading or trailing space.
#   target      cargo test target: async_generator | cli | perf. Closed set;
#               adding `tests/<name>.rs` without extending `TestTarget` fails
#               the hygiene tests.
#   test        libtest name WITHIN that target. `cli` is the target name, not a
#               module, so its names are rooted at `tests/cli/main.rs` and carry
#               no `cli::` prefix -- `binary_data::run_...`, not
#               `cli::binary_data::run_...`, which as a libtest filter matches
#               nothing at all.
#   state       fail | hang | ignored | unfilled. Closed set, parsed into an
#               enum; anything else is a hard parse error.
#   owner_task  T<NN>, backed by a real `tasks/<NN>-*.md`. Checked.
#   reason      Why this outcome is expected. No tabs.
#   evidence    A path, or a path plus a symbol. Deliberately NOT a line number:
#               line numbers rot silently and this ledger already lost one file
#               to a silent rot. CHECKED: the first whitespace-separated token
#               must resolve under the repo root and must not start with
#               `target/`. A gitignored citation is unverifiable on anyone
#               else's checkout, which is the exact failure mode this ledger
#               exists to end -- and this column carried one.
# target
cli
column5: Rung 1c is 17 of 20 chunks and 503 of 610 executing tests at this head, so the failing set for the remainder is still unknown. language is the one chunk that has never produced a verdict at any head in four batches: as a single 105-test libtest process it was OOM-SIGKILLed three times in batch 6 at t+1200 s after 66, 75 and 75 tests, with avail falling monotonically from 8.5 GiB to 1.14 GiB, and the two runner knobs were measured to be no lever (per-tier cache limits bound disk not RSS; PORFFOR_CPU_PERCENT is overridden inside run_chunk) while --test-threads below 3 is banned. Batch 7 therefore split tests/cli/language.rs into language 45 + language_errors 29 + language_numerics 31, taking the chunk set from 18 to 20 so the same 105 tests run as three separate processes; those three have banked nothing yet. All 105 were measured green at the batch-6 head, but by the UNION of a 75-test chunk attempt and a standalone 30-name tail, and a union is not the banked verdict this row's own text sets as the standard. regexp is separately stale: banked at 33 while tests/cli/regexp.rs now declares 35, so the counts sidecar re-runs it. Recount at this head with the exact-line awk is 619 test attributes, 8 spec-exec-oracle gated in frontend.rs and one heap ignore, hence 611 compiled and 610 executing -- derived from the gate count, not confirmed with --list, because the write lane runs no cargo. The only declared non-pass outcome across the 503 is the T05 heap ignore, which already has its row. Deleting this row now would declare a complete expected-failure set over three chunks that have never run, so batch 7 bumps CURRENT_BATCH to 7 and extends this header to batch-8 in one patch, both visible one-line diffs. DELETE this row rather than filling it the moment language, language_errors and language_numerics all bank green: the surviving set is then empty, and the deadline check is not evaluated at all once no unfilled row exists.

column5: Wall-clock acceptance benchmark that intentionally fails until the runtime/program split lands. Before this ledger it was an expected failure with a reason but no owner, no expiry and no record anywhere -- exactly the shape AGENTS.md rules out. It stays ignored: it is a timing acceptance gate, not a correctness test.
